chunks: A group narrated to us, from Abi al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani, from Abu Naeem Nasr ibn Isaam ibn al-Mughira al-Fahri, known as Qarqaara, who said: Abu Saeed al-Muraghi narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us
that he asked Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) about the Master of this Affair, so he gestured with his hand, meaning he is alive and his neck has hardened.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: Master of the Command (referring to the Imam/Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Askari mean when he gestured regarding the Master of the Command?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Ahmad ibn Ishaq inquires of Imam Hasan al-Askari (AS) regarding the identity of the Master of the Command, to which the Imam gestures to signify the Mahdi's continued existence. The descriptor 'ghalith al-riqba' (hardened neck) is interpreted by Shia scholars as denoting steadfastness and endurance during the period of occultation, affirming his living presence despite the delay in his reappearance.
